# VML page picture backgrounds

Original controls generated by `tools/page_picture_background_fixture.py` using
manually authored VML, a twelve-color image generated with Pillow, and a two-page
Arial document. No corpus art is included. `frame96`, `frame192`, `tile96`,
`tile192` and `recolor96` isolate fill type, embedded DPI and the recolor flag.
Each native PDF was exported by the reference application.

`tools/record_page_picture_background.py` records source/PDF hashes, native PDF
pattern dimensions and rendered color samples across both pages. Native findings:

- Frame backgrounds repeat at 600 source pixels/inch, ignoring embedded DPI.
- Explicit tiles use intrinsic DPI and round each physical tile dimension up to
  a 600-DPI pixel. PNG density rounding is observable in the 192-DPI case.
- Repetition starts at each page's top-left corner.
- The frame recolor flag and color2 do not alter these saved image pixels.
  Part 4 §19.1.2.5 describes recolor as identifying an image fill, not a command
  to apply a second color transform to the stored image.

Part 4 §§19.1.2.2 and 19.1.2.5 define VML background/fill. §19.1.3.4 describes
frame as stretching an image to its shape. The reference application's repeating page-background
behavior is a native divergence; these controls demonstrate it independently.
The 600-DPI findings describe the retained native reference PDF references, not a guarantee
about all printers or reference export devices.

The importer accepts embedded PNG/JPEG frame/tile backgrounds with the validated
metadata subset. Other fills, transform/opacity attributes, external links and
invalid media stay guarded. Native calibration for other image types, alpha
background compositing and other VML fill options remains outside this control.
Unit tests cover editing, margin changes, removal, solid-color replacement,
export/reopen, exact undo, section propagation and malformed input. Browser tests
check native sample colors across pages, editing, undo and export/reopen. Solid
page backgrounds, page borders and shared image handling have separate regressions.
